features.name: Cron test fails when the unit suite crosses midnight UTC
features.description: test/cronScheduler.test.ts:819 ("cron with both schedule and repeatEvery uses schedule for nextRun") expects the next midnight to be more than 60 s away and fails when the unit suite crosses 23:59 UTC: sandbox run artifacts/test-sandbox/2026-11-12T23-56-09.256Z/ in the agent-skills worktree, unit 11739 pass / 1 fail at 23:59:13 UTC. Reproduce first (a deterministic test that fails at 23:59:xx), then fix with an injected clock or a schedule that cannot be less than 60 s away, without weakening what the test asserts.
features.evidence: 2026-11-13, base bfa290c7; lands in the commit that adds this entry. bun run test:sandbox green on tree 691c4ca1 (unit 11788 / 0 / 402, tcp 553 / 0 / 0, embedded 349 / 0 / 0; artifacts/test-sandbox/2026-11-13T11-54-30.328Z/), the only change after it being this state update; skeptic PASS. Host checks before the gate: , gates pending. 2026-11-13, base bfa290c7, uncommitted (staged). Root cause in the test, not the scheduler: it read the real clock and required the next midnight of '0 0 * * *' (local time, as Bun.cron.parse computes a schedule without timezone) to be more than 60 s away, false during the last minute of the day. Reproduction: the unchanged assertion under setSystemTime with TZ=UTC fails at 23:59:13 and 23:59:30 UTC (received 1794528000000 = 2026-11-13T00:00:00Z, expected more than 60 s later) and passes at 12:00 UTC (1 pass / 2 fail). Fix: the test pins the clock with setSystemTime at noon and at 23:59:30 local time (restored in finally) and asserts the exact next midnight and that nextRun is not now + repeatEvery, stricter than the old lower bound; no src/ change. Docs: docs/testing.md test hygiene (clock pinning for calendar-relative assertions), changelog [Unreleased] Testing. features.name: Deprecated public APIs kept for compatibility: decide before a major version
features.description: Found by dead-code-sweep (2026-11-13, base bfa290c7). Each item still works for users, so the release-compatibility rule keeps it; removing any of them is a breaking change for a major version and needs the owner's decision, an Upgrade note with the migration, and for wire items every official SDK in sdk/ on the replacement first. Queue: Shard.queueState, a backward-compatibility getter over LimiterManager.getStateMap() with no reader in src/, public through QueueManager.getShards() (package export ./queue). Client: the deprecated re-export modules src/client/tcpClient.ts and src/client/sandboxedWorker.ts (internal, but src/client/index.ts, tcpPool.ts, queue-events/tcpSubscription.ts and test/repro-runtime-mode-parity.test.ts import them; src/client/queue.ts and worker.ts carry the same tag but are the canonical files that ./queue and ./worker resolve to); FlowProducer.disconnect() and QueueEvents.disconnect() (aliases of close(), BullMQ v5); FlowProducer.addChain / addBulkThen and their types in flowTypes.ts (legacy bunqueue flow API); the flow.ts type re-exports FlowStep, FlowResult and the others (replacement ./flowTypes); Queue.removeDlqJobAsync() (alias of removeDlqJob()); the parentId job option (legacy flow forward reference); HealthConfig.maxCommandTimeouts optional with default 3. Config and CLI: the env aliases MAX_COMPLETED_JOBS and COMPLETED_RETENTION_MS (replacements BUNQUEUE_MAX_COMPLETED_JOBS, BUNQUEUE_COMPLETED_RETENTION_MS), the HOST / BQ_HOST and BQ_DATA_PATH / DATA_PATH / SQLITE_PATH fallbacks, the LegacyTolerance warnings for values accepted before 2.9.11 (src/config/numbers.ts, envSetting.ts, settings.ts, schemaFields.ts), the CLI alias backup create (replacement backup now). Wire and HTTP: the WebSocket legacy event format for clients that never Subscribe (wsHandler.ts), the empty HTTP body read as {} (httpEndpoints.ts), the legacy TCP replies (broker-wide metrics, not found, the ambiguous Cancel refusal, WaitJob timing) in commands/monitoring.ts, handlers/management.ts, job/cancellation.ts, client/jobRemoval.ts and job-wait/brokerWait.ts. MCP: the legacy error and result payloads (resultSchemas.ts, toolResults.ts, types/adapter.ts) and the bunqueue_wait_for_job tool (bunqueue_observe_job covers the new behavior). TypeScript SDK (sdk/typescript): the ./legacy entry, Queue.disconnect() and waitJobUntilFinished() (replacements close(), waitForJob), the 0.2.2 option-coercion helpers (legacy-coercion.ts, flow-plan-legacy.ts, LEGACY.md). Internal but kept by dead-code-sweep: CronSchedulerConfig.checkIntervalMs (deprecated no-op; twelve test constructor calls pass it, in files that cron-test-midnight-boundary edits), UniqueKeyManager.register() and Shard.registerUniqueKey() (legacy without TTL; production uses registerWithTtl, the tests still call them), DlqManager getDlqJobs() (backs QueueManager.getDlq()), UniqueKeyManager.getMap() and SseHandler.getClients() (still read). Never removable while upgrades from older versions are supported: the readers and migrations of old stored data (normalizeLegacyJobPayload, legacyNameMigration.ts and SQLite migrations v31 and v32, jobOptionsBlob.ts, the PostgreSQL legacy_head_floor and flow-failure maintenance, the stored job.stalled webhook event, old timestamp and state values on rows).

features.name: Reload the TLS certificate on SIGHUP without a restart

Host checks before the gate: , gates pending. 2026-11-13, base bfa290c7, uncommitted (staged). Root cause in the test, not the broker: it asserted completedAt.size === 100 the moment the last waitUntilFinished resolved, but the broker wakes a held WaitJob while it applies the worker's ACKB (handleAckBatch replies after ackBatchWithResults), and the Worker emits 'completed' only after the ACKB reply reaches its own connection (processor.ts), so the last waits can resolve first; worker ACKs are batched by 10, matching the observed 80 and 90. Reproduction on the macOS host (load average about 21 from other sessions): unchanged test -t '100 waits' --rerun-each 30 failed 1 / 30 (received 90); with 18 extra 'yes' busy loops --rerun-each 40 failed 2 / 40 (received 90 both times). A diagnostic copy (scratchpad, not committed) that keeps polling after the waits resolved found the count short in 3 / 40 runs (90 each) and 100 events in 40 / 40 runs, the missing ones about 0.1 ms after the last wait, p90 delay at most 2.1 ms: no notification is lost. Fix: the test waits up to 5 s (polling every 5 ms) for all 100 worker events, then asserts the same two things, size 100 and p90 delay under 400 ms; every delay now uses a real event timestamp.
